top.title: ‘Name National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka’ – Brymo to Tinubu
top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian singer, Brymo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to name the National Theatre after late veteran actor Pete Edochie instead of Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, following the death of the Nollywood icon. Brymo made the appeal in a video shared on his official Instagram page on Wednesday, where he paid tribute to Edochie and called on the President to reconsider the naming of the national cultural landmark. “Dear President Tinubu, name the National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka, please,” the singer said. He also celebrated the late actor, saying, “Cheers to one of the greatest men, Pete Edochie. May you live forever in our hearts, and on our screens.” Edochie died at the age of 79, with his death announced on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. His passing has prompted tributes from political leaders, colleagues and members of the entertainment industry. President Tinubu, in a tribute, described the late actor as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians and a pioneer of Nigeria’s film industry. He also recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart in the 1980s. The President praised his performances in productions including Igodo , Rituals and Lionheart , saying his work helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences around the world. Brymo’s appeal comes against the backdrop of the Federal Government’s decision to rename the National Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos, after Soyinka in 2024, as part of the celebration of the literary icon’s 90th birthday. Tinubu announced that the facility would be known as the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts. The renovated complex was formally commissioned under the new name on October 1, 2025, during Nigeria’s 65th Independence anniversary celebrations. The President had described the renaming as an honour for Soyinka, whose contributions to literature, theatre and human rights advocacy have earned him international recognition, including the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature. top.title: Thousands will hit Houston streets for Turkey Trot races on Thanksgiving. What to know.
top.description: People run during the BakerRipley Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving morning, Thursday, Nov. 25, 2021, through the Galleria area in Houston. (Mark Mulligan/Staff photographer) Thousands of Turkey Trot runners will hit the streets across Houston Thursday morning before the Thanksgiving festivities begin. The Turkey Trot is a Thanksgiving race tradition dating back to the 1890s that has grown to become the biggest running day of the year, according to RunSignUp.com, which tracks annual stats. There are 66 scheduled events in Texas on Thanksgiving Day on FindARace.com . Houston hosts three large races. Beyond Houston, several Turkey Trots are scheduled across the surrounding area, including races in Katy, The Woodlands, Kingwood, Sugar Land, Pearland and Friendswood. Tips for running a Turkey Trot race Dr. Larry Balle, a sports medicine physician at Houston Methodist, has some tips for getting through the turkey trot, whether you're a first-timer or a regular runner. Stay hydrated, get enough sleep and avoid working out too hard the day before the race For regular runners: "You cannot make up for missed training in the final few days. If you have been running regularly, trust the work you have already put in. Keep your runs easy, stay hydrated and well-fueled, get plenty of sleep, and resist the temptation to fit in one last hard workout." For newbies: "If you're new to running, don't feel pressured to run the entire race. Alternating between running and walking is perfectly acceptable and may help prevent injury or excessive fatigue. Finishing comfortably is a worthwhile goal." Be sure to warm up on race morning With cooler weather arriving in Houston, Thanksgiving morning is expected to be one of the coldest of the year, according to reports. "Five to ten minutes of brisk walking or easy jogging, along with movements such as leg swings and marching, can help prepare your body for the effort ahead," Balle said. "Wear shoes and clothing you have already used during training. Race day is not the time to try something new." Eat a familiar breakfast Balle says runners shouldn't drink large amounts of water or overcomplicate fueling the morning of the race. " A familiar breakfast such as toast, oatmeal, or a banana one to three hours beforehand may work well, depending on your stomach and start time." Keep it in control and don't push through injuries "Once the race begins, it is easy to get swept up in the crowd and start too fast," Balle said. For the 5K: "Aim for a controlled first mile so you have something left for the finish." For the 10K: " Settle into a pace you can maintain for several miles before deciding whether to pick it up." "If your goal is simply to finish, use a pace that allows you to speak in short sentences," Balle said. "There is no rule that says you have to race every mile." top.title: FG orders probe as three inmates die after Ilorin jailbreak
top.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has ordered an investigation into the deaths of three condemned inmates at the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, following a jailbreak attempt last week. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who ordered the investigation, described the deaths as unfortunate and vowed that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The minister, who visited the facility on Wednesday to assess the situation, also expressed concern that more than 70 condemned inmates at the centre had spent over 10 years on death row, attributing the prolonged stay to delays by state authorities in exercising their powers to grant clemency or commute death sentences. The minister was represented during the visit by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Sylvester Nwakuche, who briefed journalists after inspecting the facility. Nwakuche said he returned to Ilorin on the minister’s directive to investigate reports surrounding the incident and assess the condition of the facility. According to him, seven condemned inmates attempted to breach the security of the custodial centre during the jailbreak, but only two succeeded in escaping. He said the remaining five were apprehended and returned to custody, but three subsequently died. “Two succeeded in making their way out of the facility, while the remaining five could not. They were taken back, but unfortunately, we were informed that three out of the five who could not escape lost their lives. “That is an unfortunate incident, and the minister wanted us to come immediately to assess the situation,” he said. The Comptroller-General said a team had been constituted to investigate the deaths, adding that the inquiry would involve clinical, medical and intelligence processes. He assured that the two escaped inmates would be rearrested, regardless of how long it took. Nwakuche also disclosed that more than 70 condemned inmates were being held at the Oke-Kura facility, with some having spent over a decade on death row. He described the situation as a major challenge, noting that the colonial-era facility was accommodating nearly 685 inmates and was severely overcrowded. He said the problem extended beyond Ilorin, disclosing that more than 4,000 inmates were on death row across correctional facilities nationwide. The Comptroller-General appealed to state governors to exercise their constitutional powers by considering the commutation of death sentences to life imprisonment, where appropriate. According to him, such action would enable the Correctional Service to transfer affected inmates to less congested facilities, where they could undergo rehabilitation and vocational training. “We have been appealing to the necessary authorities, the governors, to do what the law permits them to do. Traditional Cover-0 is pure man-to-man coverage against all eligible receivers and no safety help in the middle, but this is almost like a three-deep zone variation of Cover-0. The Commanders put eight defenders on the line of scrimmage this time and all eight of them blitz. That leaves just three defenders in coverage as they effectively play the deep zones of Cover-3 behind the blitz. Burrow again looks to his top receiver in Ja’Marr Chase, but this time Chase is in the slot and spotting up as a hot route option. Burrow immediately pulls the trigger to avoid a sack and throws hot to Chase, but cornerback Rasul Douglas plays this perfectly. Douglas sits at the first down marker knowing the ball has to come out quick against the blitz. He knows Chase is Burrow’s go-to target and he spots Chase beginning to slow down and spot up underneath. So before Burrow even delivers the throw, Douglas begins breaking on the pass. This enables Douglas to arrive at Chase before the ball does and he goes over the top of him to nearly intercept the pass. The Commanders defense had an outstanding performance against the Bengals on Monday night. top.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
top.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

top.title: Phillies lose third baseman Alec Bohm to free agency, signs with Royals
top.description: The Phillies have lost their most consistent right-hand hitting run producer to free agency. Often-maligned corner infielder Alec Bohm has agreed to a two-year, $20 million contract with the Kansas Royals, it was reported Wednesday morning. Over seven seasons, mostly spent as the Phillies third baseman, Bohm fashioned a .273 batting average. Despite only hitting .249 in 2026, Bohm finished second on the club with 88 runs batted in, posting one of the National League's higher marks for two-out hits with men in scoring position. Bohm added 15 home runs and 29 doubles in 155 games the past season. He had an on-base percentage of .315 and a .383 slugging percentage. Bohm was a minus-0.2 WAR last season, in part due to being considered an inconsistent defender as well as slow on the basepaths. The 30-year-old shifted to first base after the Phillies acquired Luis Arraez and rearranged their infield which moved Bryce Harper from first to right field. The third overall pick in the 2018 draft out of Wichita State, Bohm is fifth all-time for games played at third base for the Phillies. He was an All-Star selection in 2024, when he hit hit .280 and drove in 97 and smacked 44 doubles. He also had 97 RBIS in 2023, a campaign that featured a career-high 20 home runs. The club was rumored to have put Bohm on the trade block multiple times in recent seasons, but no specific offers were reported and he remained an everyday fixture at Citizens Bank Park. On April 11, 2022, in a home game against the New York Mets , Bohm was caught on TV saying, "I ----ing hate this place," after fans sarcastically cheered him for making a routine play following three throwing errors. He later apologized for his remark. The Phillies have prospect Aidan Miller as Bohm's potential replacement at third base. He was ESPN's No. 10 overall prospect heading into 2026, but missed almost the entire season with a back injury before returning for four games and then playing in the Arizona Fall League. Another option is Bryson Stott, who shifted to third from second base after the Arraez acquisition. top.title: Williams exceeded F1 cost cap by £627,000
top.description: Williams have had a difficult 2026 - uncompetitive and now in breach of spending rules [Getty Images] Williams broke Formula 1's cost cap during the 2025 season, governing body the FIA has found. The team say they "unintentionally" exceeded the cap by £627,000. Last season, the spending limit was $135m (£106m). Alpine were also found to have broken the rules, although theirs was a procedural breach without overspending. Both teams have reached so-called 'accepted breach agreements' with the FIA. Williams' involves a financial penalty, the amount of which has not been disclosed, and a 1.5% reduction in permitted aerodynamic research and development time for the next 12 months. Alpine have also been given an undisclosed financial penalty. Both teams must foot the costs of the investigations by the FIA into their rule-breaking. A Williams statement said: "The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. "We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap. "The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted co-operatively and in good faith throughout the review process. "Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future." The FIA said in a statement: "There is no accusation or evidence that (Williams) sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the cost-cap administration. "The financial regulations are complex, and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted by (Williams) in good faith. "Williams has accepted the FIA's interpretation and the resulting breaches." It said Williams' breach was the equivalent of a 0.48% overspend, which "falls at the lower end of the less than 5% minor overspend range". Williams' costs were incurred as the team tried to update their operations in order to become more competitive. nigeria.title: ‘Name National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka’ – Brymo to Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian singer, Brymo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to name the National Theatre after late veteran actor Pete Edochie instead of Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, following the death of the Nollywood icon. Brymo made the appeal in a video shared on his official Instagram page on Wednesday, where he paid tribute to Edochie and called on the President to reconsider the naming of the national cultural landmark. “Dear President Tinubu, name the National Theatre after Pete Edochie, not Wole Soyinka, please,” the singer said. He also celebrated the late actor, saying, “Cheers to one of the greatest men, Pete Edochie. May you live forever in our hearts, and on our screens.” Edochie died at the age of 79, with his death announced on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. His passing has prompted tributes from political leaders, colleagues and members of the entertainment industry. President Tinubu, in a tribute, described the late actor as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians and a pioneer of Nigeria’s film industry. He also recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart in the 1980s. The President praised his performances in productions including Igodo , Rituals and Lionheart , saying his work helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences around the world. Brymo’s appeal comes against the backdrop of the Federal Government’s decision to rename the National Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos, after Soyinka in 2024, as part of the celebration of the literary icon’s 90th birthday. Tinubu announced that the facility would be known as the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts. The renovated complex was formally commissioned under the new name on October 1, 2025, during Nigeria’s 65th Independence anniversary celebrations. The President had described the renaming as an honour for Soyinka, whose contributions to literature, theatre and human rights advocacy have earned him international recognition, including the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature. nigeria.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has ordered an investigation into the deaths of three condemned inmates at the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, following a jailbreak attempt last week. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who ordered the investigation, described the deaths as unfortunate and vowed that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law. The minister, who visited the facility on Wednesday to assess the situation, also expressed concern that more than 70 condemned inmates at the centre had spent over 10 years on death row, attributing the prolonged stay to delays by state authorities in exercising their powers to grant clemency or commute death sentences. The minister was represented during the visit by the Comptroller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Sylvester Nwakuche, who briefed journalists after inspecting the facility. Nwakuche said he returned to Ilorin on the minister’s directive to investigate reports surrounding the incident and assess the condition of the facility. According to him, seven condemned inmates attempted to breach the security of the custodial centre during the jailbreak, but only two succeeded in escaping. He said the remaining five were apprehended and returned to custody, but three subsequently died. “Two succeeded in making their way out of the facility, while the remaining five could not. They were taken back, but unfortunately, we were informed that three out of the five who could not escape lost their lives. “That is an unfortunate incident, and the minister wanted us to come immediately to assess the situation,” he said. The Comptroller-General said a team had been constituted to investigate the deaths, adding that the inquiry would involve clinical, medical and intelligence processes. He assured that the two escaped inmates would be rearrested, regardless of how long it took. Nwakuche also disclosed that more than 70 condemned inmates were being held at the Oke-Kura facility, with some having spent over a decade on death row. He described the situation as a major challenge, noting that the colonial-era facility was accommodating nearly 685 inmates and was severely overcrowded. He said the problem extended beyond Ilorin, disclosing that more than 4,000 inmates were on death row across correctional facilities nationwide. The Comptroller-General appealed to state governors to exercise their constitutional powers by considering the commutation of death sentences to life imprisonment, where appropriate. According to him, such action would enable the Correctional Service to transfer affected inmates to less congested facilities, where they could undergo rehabilitation and vocational training. “We have been appealing to the necessary authorities, the governors, to do what the law permits them to do. He added that some vehicles in the convoy were observed without registration numbers or with questionable number plates, while sirens were also used in violation of applicable traffic regulations. Usman said the Command condemned the conduct, warning that political activities must not degenerate into thuggery, violence or inflammatory statements. He said the Police would not tolerate any action capable of undermining public peace or setting a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Command urged the party’s leadership to honour its commitment to peaceful political engagement and cooperate with security agencies, including handing over individuals involved in unlawful conduct. Usman said the three suspects had been charged to court for prosecution, adding that any breach of agreed security protocols or applicable laws would be dealt with accordingly. The committee was told that 130 police officers and 1,600 stewards would be deployed. Some 450 stewards will be assigned to spectators seated on the stadium pitch. Measures to address concerns include additional early-morning trains, noise monitoring and no external public address system. Breathalysers will be used at stadium entrances for spectators who appear intoxicated. Committee chair Grace Ferguson-Thorne said the security arrangements, stewarding levels and planned closure of the stadium roof were “really reassuring”. The Principality Stadium has hosted late-night boxing before. Joe Calzaghe’s 2007 victory over Mikkel Kessler began at about 2am to suit US television audiences. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets. The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing new charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts. U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts. “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.” More than $1 billion in crypto frozen Crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts. The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, says its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims. The FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department said. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds. “The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. Scam cases tied to fake crypto platforms In the past month alone, the Criminal Division filed or unsealed charges against more than 30 scam defendants, including those tied to Southeast Asian scam centers running crypto investment fraud schemes. Other cases involved inheritance fraud, jury duty imposters working from Georgia prisons and sweepstakes schemes aimed at elderly Americans. The Secret Service said it has restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds during the surge. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine HRF Announces Funding of Seven Bitcoin Projects for People Living Under Authoritarian Regimes The Human Rights Foundation (HRF) is pleased to announce grants from its Bitcoin Development Fund for seven projects advancing bitcoin self-custody, financial privacy, and education for people living under authoritarian regimes. One project translates bitcoin terminology into 21 African languages. Another mines bitcoin with surplus solar power in rural Nigerian homes, paying it directly to the households that generate it. Others build tools for people facing repression anywhere — activists who need to find and fix the privacy leaks in their bitcoin use, communities who need self-custody devices built from parts found in any electronics store, observers who need election evidence preserved before it disappears, and people who need to turn an ordinary phone into an offline Bitcoin wallet. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Next Technology (NXTT) Sells 500 Bitcoin to Fund AI Push Next Technology Holding (Nasdaq: NXTT) sold about 500 bitcoin last week and said it will put the money toward artificial intelligence projects, the latest public company to trim its bitcoin treasury as prices slide. The Japan-based software firm disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday that it sold the coins on Nov. 21 for about $29.22 million. That works out to an average price of $58,468.11 per bitcoin, net of fees and expenses. The sale leaves NXTT with 5,333 BTC. The company was paid in tether (USDT), the dollar-pegged stablecoin, rather than in dollars. NXTT said it plans to use the proceeds for research and development of its AI-related initiatives, including its AI software products and services, as well as for general corporate purposes. A shift away from buying The sale is the first under a program the company’s board approved on Oct. 30. That program allows NXTT to sell or pledge its bitcoin “from time to time in one or more tranches,” through exchange sales, block trades or loans that use the coins as collateral, with the stated aim of “reducing risk exposure and enhancing liquidity.” The filing also repeats a line from the company’s latest quarterly report that marks a clear break from its earlier approach. NXTT “does not currently expect to purchase additional Bitcoin,” the company said, adding that it has adjusted its strategy to focus on managing the coins it already holds. The program has no expiration date and doesn’t require the company to sell any set amount. The board can change, pause or end it at any time. As of Nov. 24, NXTT said it had not pledged any of its bitcoin as collateral. How NXTT built its stack NXTT, which is incorporated in Wyoming but based in Saitama Prefecture, Japan, describes itself as running two strategies: AI-enabled software development and holding bitcoin. It keeps substantially all of its coins with Japan-based institutional custodians, according to its quarterly filing . The company held 833 BTC at the end of 2024 and added 5,000 BTC in 2025, bringing its total to 5,833 BTC. Its filing puts the cost basis of those coins at about $183.1 million, or roughly $31,400 per bitcoin, meaning last week’s sale still came in well above what the company paid on average. Falling prices have still hit the books. NXTT reported a net loss of $32.2 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared with net income of $295.1 million a year earlier. The company said the swing came mainly from a drop in the fair value of its digital assets. The company has also been reshaping its leadership around AI. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine France’s Senate Rejects Rule Forcing Bitcoin Holders to Declare Self-Custody Wallets France’s Senate has rejected a proposal that would have forced bitcoin holders to report self-custody wallets worth €100,000 or more to the tax authorities, along with two other crypto tax measures in the 2027 budget. Senators voted down two identical amendments on Nov. 24 during debate on the first part of the 2027 finance bill. Both would have required taxpayers to declare crypto wallets they hold directly, outside a crypto service provider, when the total value inside reached at least €100,000 on Dec. 31 of the tax year. The first, amendment I-2447 , came from Sens. Pascal Savoldelli and Pierre Barros and the Communist-led CRCE-K group. The second, amendment I-2992 , came from Sen. Anne-Sophie Romagny and seven other senators. The government opposed both, and both were rejected. The case for a wallet rule in France Backers argued that France already makes taxpayers declare accounts on foreign crypto platforms, just like foreign bank accounts. Wallets that holders manage themselves, without an intermediary, escape any such obligation. “They have become the digital equivalent of the undeclared safe,” the CRCE-K group wrote in its amendment, adding that tax authorities can’t see them, check gains on them or reach them in an estate or when a holder moves abroad. Romagny’s version pointed to a gap in the numbers. Crypto holders in France realized €3.5 billion in gains in 2021, but only €400 million in digital assets were declared to the tax administration that same year, the amendment said. It proposed fines of up to €10,000 for failing to declare. The National Assembly had approved the same wallet rule on Nov. 3. It fell away the next day, when deputies rejected the entire revenue section of the budget. Senators then took up the same measure as an amendment to the budget. Stablecoin swaps and exit tax also rejected Senators also rejected two other proposals from the CRCE-K group. Amendment I-2421 would have ended France’s tax deferral on swaps into electronic money tokens under the EU’s MiCA rules. That would have made converting bitcoin into a regulated stablecoin a taxable event. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. sports.description: People run during the BakerRipley Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving morning, Thursday, Nov. 25, 2021, through the Galleria area in Houston. (Mark Mulligan/Staff photographer) Thousands of Turkey Trot runners will hit the streets across Houston Thursday morning before the Thanksgiving festivities begin. The Turkey Trot is a Thanksgiving race tradition dating back to the 1890s that has grown to become the biggest running day of the year, according to RunSignUp.com, which tracks annual stats. There are 66 scheduled events in Texas on Thanksgiving Day on FindARace.com . Houston hosts three large races. Beyond Houston, several Turkey Trots are scheduled across the surrounding area, including races in Katy, The Woodlands, Kingwood, Sugar Land, Pearland and Friendswood. Tips for running a Turkey Trot race Dr. Larry Balle, a sports medicine physician at Houston Methodist, has some tips for getting through the turkey trot, whether you're a first-timer or a regular runner. Stay hydrated, get enough sleep and avoid working out too hard the day before the race For regular runners: "You cannot make up for missed training in the final few days. If you have been running regularly, trust the work you have already put in. Keep your runs easy, stay hydrated and well-fueled, get plenty of sleep, and resist the temptation to fit in one last hard workout." For newbies: "If you're new to running, don't feel pressured to run the entire race. Alternating between running and walking is perfectly acceptable and may help prevent injury or excessive fatigue. Finishing comfortably is a worthwhile goal." Be sure to warm up on race morning With cooler weather arriving in Houston, Thanksgiving morning is expected to be one of the coldest of the year, according to reports. "Five to ten minutes of brisk walking or easy jogging, along with movements such as leg swings and marching, can help prepare your body for the effort ahead," Balle said. "Wear shoes and clothing you have already used during training. Race day is not the time to try something new." Eat a familiar breakfast Balle says runners shouldn't drink large amounts of water or overcomplicate fueling the morning of the race. " A familiar breakfast such as toast, oatmeal, or a banana one to three hours beforehand may work well, depending on your stomach and start time." Keep it in control and don't push through injuries "Once the race begins, it is easy to get swept up in the crowd and start too fast," Balle said. For the 5K: "Aim for a controlled first mile so you have something left for the finish." For the 10K: " Settle into a pace you can maintain for several miles before deciding whether to pick it up." "If your goal is simply to finish, use a pace that allows you to speak in short sentences," Balle said. "There is no rule that says you have to race every mile." sports.title: Phillies lose third baseman Alec Bohm to free agency, signs with Royals
sports.description: The Phillies have lost their most consistent right-hand hitting run producer to free agency. Often-maligned corner infielder Alec Bohm has agreed to a two-year, $20 million contract with the Kansas Royals, it was reported Wednesday morning. Over seven seasons, mostly spent as the Phillies third baseman, Bohm fashioned a .273 batting average. Despite only hitting .249 in 2026, Bohm finished second on the club with 88 runs batted in, posting one of the National League's higher marks for two-out hits with men in scoring position. Bohm added 15 home runs and 29 doubles in 155 games the past season. He had an on-base percentage of .315 and a .383 slugging percentage. Bohm was a minus-0.2 WAR last season, in part due to being considered an inconsistent defender as well as slow on the basepaths. The 30-year-old shifted to first base after the Phillies acquired Luis Arraez and rearranged their infield which moved Bryce Harper from first to right field. The third overall pick in the 2018 draft out of Wichita State, Bohm is fifth all-time for games played at third base for the Phillies. He was an All-Star selection in 2024, when he hit hit .280 and drove in 97 and smacked 44 doubles. He also had 97 RBIS in 2023, a campaign that featured a career-high 20 home runs. The club was rumored to have put Bohm on the trade block multiple times in recent seasons, but no specific offers were reported and he remained an everyday fixture at Citizens Bank Park. On April 11, 2022, in a home game against the New York Mets , Bohm was caught on TV saying, "I ----ing hate this place," after fans sarcastically cheered him for making a routine play following three throwing errors. He later apologized for his remark. The Phillies have prospect Aidan Miller as Bohm's potential replacement at third base. He was ESPN's No. 10 overall prospect heading into 2026, but missed almost the entire season with a back injury before returning for four games and then playing in the Arizona Fall League. Another option is Bryson Stott, who shifted to third from second base after the Arraez acquisition. The team say they "unintentionally" exceeded the cap by £627,000. Last season, the spending limit was $135m (£106m). Alpine were also found to have broken the rules, although theirs was a procedural breach without overspending. Both teams have reached so-called 'accepted breach agreements' with the FIA. Williams' involves a financial penalty, the amount of which has not been disclosed, and a 1.5% reduction in permitted aerodynamic research and development time for the next 12 months. Alpine have also been given an undisclosed financial penalty. Both teams must foot the costs of the investigations by the FIA into their rule-breaking. A Williams statement said: "The breach relates to administrative costs we incurred making changes to our company structure. "We believed these costs fell outside of the cap. Following discussions with the FIA, we have agreed to resolve the matter in line with their interpretation that the costs should have been in cap. "The FIA has noted that Williams did not gain any sporting or financial advantage, and nor did we ever seek to. It has also noted that we acted co-operatively and in good faith throughout the review process. "Integrity is central to what Williams stands for and we can now close this case and remain focused on our future." The FIA said in a statement: "There is no accusation or evidence that (Williams) sought at any time to act in bad faith, dishonestly or in a fraudulent manner, nor that it wilfully concealed any information from the cost-cap administration. "The financial regulations are complex, and the breaches arose from an interpretation adopted by (Williams) in good faith. "Williams has accepted the FIA's interpretation and the resulting breaches." It said Williams' breach was the equivalent of a 0.48% overspend, which "falls at the lower end of the less than 5% minor overspend range". Williams' costs were incurred as the team tried to update their operations in order to become more competitive. sports.title: 'Justice for sport' - reaction to Afcon final verdict
sports.description: Senegal's football federation reacted to the Cas verdict on social media with a picture of the side lifting the Afcon trophy alongside the caption "again and always champions of Africa" [Getty Images] "Justice for sport." That was the initial reaction of Senegal football federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall to the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate the West Africans as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions. The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final but were stripped of the title in March by a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board, which imposed a 3-0 forfeit after they walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded against them when the game was goalless. Following a hearing in Lausanne in October, a three-man Cas panel unanimously overturned that ruling by Caf, effectively judging that the decisions taken by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala in restarting the match and playing it to a conclusion were final. Morocco's football federation (FRMF), however, says it will "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision". The North Africans could yet take their fight to the Swiss Federal Court. Those in Senegal have celebrated the return of the title, while several legal experts have backed the Cas verdict. Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling Teranga Lions pay tribute to fans Senegal's talisman Sadio Mane, who was named player of the tournament at Afcon 2025, said the ruling "fills us with joy". The 34-year-old former Liverpool man thanked his team-mates and Senegal staff as well as the whole Senegalese nation at home and abroad. "Your faith in us gave us strength during the most difficult moments. This victory is yours, too," he said in a statement on social media. Senegal captain Kalidou Koulibaly, who missed the final through injury, echoed that sentiment. "Some victories are won on the pitch, while others are won in the heart of a people," he said in a post on Facebook. "This one is both. "Long before this verdict, there was you - your prayers, your flags in the windows, your fervour, and the pride that unites us all: the pride of the people of Teranga." Pape Gueye, the man who scored the extra-time winner in Rabat, described the Cas decision as "an immense relief". Both he and Mane had a message of support for Morocco. "Senegal and Morocco are brotherly nations; may our shared passion for football continue to bring us closer together," Mane said. technology.title: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
technology.description: After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating. Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional." A fourth engine Nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There's WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that's where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports. technology.title: Hera probe finds DART left a stadium-sized dent in asteroid Dimorphos
technology.description: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has revealed a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA struck with its DART spacecraft in 2022. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test was deliberately crashed into the asteroid on September 26, 2022. The original plan called for a European spacecraft – Asteroid Impact Mission (AIM) – to launch first and observe the before and after effects of DART. AIM was canceled, and the Hera mission launched in 2024. DART was a success. Scientists were able to determine that the impact had indeed changed the orbit of Dimorphos. The question was what else had happened to the asteroid. Scientists spotted ejecta and debris following the DART impact, but the close-up observations by Hera have revealed the full extent of the collision. Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said: "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape or stayed the same. "Much to our surprise the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." Scientists also noted that the asteroid is now tumbling in its orbit. Hera is surveying the 151-meter-wide Dimorphos and its larger companion, the 730-meter-wide Didymos, from about 25 to 30 km away. It moves around the pair at roughly 12 cm/s, using thruster firings to trace rectangular paths rather than conventional circular orbits. The plan is to approach closer, to about 13 km, to get higher-resolution snaps. A complicating factor is the discovery that hundreds of orbiting boulders surround the asteroids. Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, said: "The team will have to take account of these objects in the coming weeks as the mission moves in closer." Hera will deploy two CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in early 2027. The Italian-led Milani will study surface composition and surrounding dust, while the Luxembourg-led Juventas will use radar to probe Dimorphos's interior before attempting a landing. Scientists also want to measure Dimorphos's mass. Combined with the observed change in its orbit, that will help them assess how effectively DART transferred momentum to the asteroid and improve predictions for future deflection attempts. Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli said: "NASA's DART mission demonstrated that we can change an asteroid's orbit. Hera is now revealing what happened to the asteroid itself. By combining these two missions, humanity is taking a decisive step towards making asteroid deflection a reliable tool for protecting our planet." ®

technology.title: Microsoft's NTLM security changes trip up third-party logins
technology.description: Microsoft's November security updates can break authentication in some third-party applications and devices following changes to NTLM message signing. Affected systems include authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) products, and application packaging tools, the company's support notice says. The failures stem from products that claim to supply required information during NTLM authentication but return incomplete or empty data, Microsoft said: "An affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field." Administrators can use the notice's network trace and event log examples to identify affected products. For confirmed cases, the temporary workaround is to set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm Registry value to 1 on affected clients. This stops the client offering signing, backing out the new default rather than fixing the incompatible product. The recommended long-term options are a vendor update or Kerberos authentication, where supported. The value sits under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 and defaults to 0, enabling clients to offer signing on non-anonymous connections. The NTLM changes arrived in the November 10 update as phase 1 in a 2-phase process. In phase 1, "Windows client devices begin offering NTLM signing on all connections by default. Servers accept both signed and unsigned clients. Auditing events identify clients not using signing." Phase 2, scheduled for May 2027, will make Windows servers require NTLM signing by default. "Clients that do not offer signing will be rejected by secure servers," Microsoft stated. Ominously, Microsoft warned that it "might remove the registry keys at a future date," so the company is not kidding about the temporary workaround thing. The additional protections were added to address CVE-2026-118737 , a vulnerability in which "improper verification of cryptographic signature in Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network." NTLM is on Microsoft's hit list, having joined the Deprecated Features list in 2024. It dates back to the era of Windows NT, and Microsoft has made clear that it wants customers to move to Kerberos, which became the default in 2000. Even so, NTLM lingers on. Deprecation doesn't remove Microsoft's obligation to secure NTLM while it remains in supported Windows releases. For administrators, though, the immediate task is identifying incompatible products before temporary exceptions give way to stricter enforcement. ®

technology.title: US Treasury financial crimes unit becomes latest fed breach victim
technology.description: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has taken some systems offline following unauthorized access, disrupting regulatory filings for financial institutions. An alert has gone up on FinCEN's Bank Secrecy Act E-Filing website, as shown in this archived copy , informing those who need to submit reports that they might not be able to while the agency deals with the situation. FinCEN not only enforces compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act and associated regulations but also collects and analyzes financial intelligence for sharing with other US agencies and foreign government partners. In other words, it has some juicy info in its databases. “FinCEN is investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems,” the alert states. “As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline.” FinCEN hasn't said which systems intruders accessed, but clues in the deadline extension notice the agency posted alongside the warning suggest the disruption affects its reporting services for banks and other financial institutions required to submit reports detailing certain financial transactions and suspicious activity that may indicate money laundering or other illicit activity. FinCEN's Secure Data Transfer Mode, one method of submitting those reports, appears to be affected, as do services companies use to submit beneficial ownership information reports and individuals use to update their FinCEN identifiers. Eligible organizations and individuals with filings or updates due from November 18 through December 29 now have until December 30 to submit them. The Register has learned that there’s no evidence of any unauthorized access to Bank Secrecy Act data or beneficial ownership databases. That said, the investigation is ongoing - so that could change. “Treasury is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and third-party forensic examiners to determine the scope and impact of the incident,” a FinCEN official told us in an email. Several US government agencies have experienced cybersecurity incidents in recent months, including the ATF and the FBI , and reports emerged this week that intruders had also compromised an unclassified CIA system . While US authorities have linked previous cyberespionage campaigns to Chinese or other government-backed groups , financially motivated criminal groups have also targeted federal agencies. As the FinCEN breach is still under investigation, the agency hasn’t stated who may be involved and for what purpose. ®

technology.title: NASA's nuclear-powered Mars delivery service takes shape
technology.description: NASA has settled key design choices for its planned nuclear-fission-powered spacecraft, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, following a mission review in October. Targeting launch in late 2028, SR-1 would be the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion and deliver a capsule carrying three helicopters to Mars. There have been some changes since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed off the concept [PDF] at the agency's Ignition event in March. Improved shielding and spacecraft design will allow a shorter boom between the reactor and the spacecraft's main body, protecting its electronics and the SkyFall payload. The shorter boom will, according to NASA, "reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design." The revised design also includes larger X-band antenna dishes to transmit data to Earth. Decisions are still pending on how many radiator panels the vehicle needs, the output power levels of the nuclear power module, and how long the reactor will operate. Currently, the mission calls for the spacecraft to start its reactor once it has left Earth orbit and gradually ramp up power. After a period during which performance data will be sent back to Earth, the reactor will be shut down until after the SkyFall capsule, containing a trio of Mars Ingenuity-class helicopters, is delivered to Martian orbit. Solar arrays will power the spacecraft during its cruise to Mars. The fission reactor will then be reactivated to let engineers collect more data on its performance in deep space. NASA also awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the nuclear power module. "Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule," the agency said. The latter part regarding the schedule is certainly a challenge . Meeting the late-2028 launch target leaves roughly two years to finish designing, building, and testing the spacecraft. ESA is also targeting late 2028 for its long-delayed Rosalind Franklin rover. Missing the intended Mars departure opportunity could push SR-1 into a later launch window, although NASA has not specified a fallback schedule. ®

technology.title: Microsoft fixes Office dialog that had nothing to say and wouldn't go away
technology.description: Microsoft has released a fix for a baffling bug that threw a blank window over Office applications and brought work to a standstill. The problem appeared when users launched an affected Office app, which could display an empty dialog box with no text and no buttons. Because the dialog offered no way to close it, some users were locked out of their work entirely, unable to continue until the issue was resolved. The good news is that there's an update to fix the problem – version 2611, build 16.0.20625.20142. The bad news is that you might not be able to launch the applications to perform the update because of that blank dialog window. Microsoft instructs affected users to save their work, close all Office applications, and open Command Prompt as administrator. They can then force the update with: "%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142 The glitch affects a swathe of Microsoft 365 products – Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, and OneNote. Users reported the problem on Microsoft's forums , where volunteer moderator Stefan Blom noted that "this seems to be a common error at the moment" and suggested users try an Office repair or the more thorough Online Repair. Online Repair reinstalls Office, however, some users reported activation and sign-in problems alongside the blank windows, which may hint at the cause. Microsoft has yet to elucidate. Other users found that rolling back Office resolved the issue, while several reported that signing in with another application, such as Edge, fixed things. For administrators preparing fleets of devices, a dialog that blocks first use creates another deployment headache. One user with E3 licensing reported: "We can't just hand off a staged machine without getting call[s] that our new users can't get Office to work because of the blank licensing window." Microsoft has shared a fix for the problem, but has not stated which versions of its productivity applications were affected, nor has it explained what went wrong. The fix is welcome. An explanation of how Office ended up blocking users with a window containing nothing at all would be welcome too. ®

The unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command. technology.title: JetBrains finds agents may cheat with open source
technology.description: JetBrains has revamped a benchmark for evaluating large language models after suspecting too many agents gamed their tasks the first time round. The company labelled this agentic practice "reward hacking" in a post summarizing the results of its revised evaluation. Like its predecessor , Kotlin Benchmark 2.0 is a collection of tasks that evaluates how well AI coding agents work with the Kotlin programming language , in order to help Kotlin programmers decide which agent-model configurations to use. The tasks include fixing tricky problems in Kotlin code across different domains, and making corrections to multiple files. Dirty data The revised benchmar k now includes 30 Kotlin multi-file code problems that have not been exposed to the public in any way before. The revised test all but guarantees that the agents have not encountered this set of problems, or potential solutions, before. Another 70 tasks are based on code that resides in public repositories. The test also blocked all network access for the open source tasks, except for what was needed to communicate with the model itself. This minimized the possibility that the agent could look for an existing answer already posted, perhaps through a patch or pull request. A 30-minute limit was set for each task. Overall, the agents were significantly less accurate when solving problems on codebases they had never encountered. Top resolution rates dropped rather suspiciously from 86.2 percent on tasks based on open source repositories to 60 percent on those based on closed source repositories. Although the agents lacked network access, JetBrains boffins theorized that they might have benefited from encountering and internalizing these open source repositories during training. Only the private repositories were completely new to them. Also curious was how a different set of models excelled at the closed source problems, compared to those models that usually did better on the open source tasks. Leaderboard Shakeup When restricted to closed source tasks, two dark horse models rose to the top: Gemini 3.8 Flash, via Antigravity CLI, topped the list with a 60 percent success rate, closely followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (running on OpenCode) at 58.9 percent. Of the two, the open weight DeepSeek was far cheaper (at $0.08 per task) than the closed weight Gemini ($1.74 per task), however. In contrast, Opus 5.5 completed only 53.3 percent of the tasks at $1.21 per task, and Fable 5.1 completed only 44.4 percent of the tasks, at a luxurious $3.27 per task. Claude Code harnessed both of these models. technology.description: Win4Wine is one of the more remarkable and creative hacks we've read about in recent years. It runs Windows XP's genuine Explorer shell through patched Wine on Debian 13, with a custom window manager integrating Linux applications into the desktop. As its GitHub repository explains: "The taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows are XP's real ones, and Linux applications get XP's frames and taskbar buttons." This impressive, possibly demented project has English installation instructions and a README, although its design documents are in Japanese. We found Mozilla's built-in translation handled those pretty well. Its developer goes by miKuta0407 on GitHub, their homepage , and X . Also note, you're going to need some Windows installation media for the full experience. The README says: "No Microsoft files are included. Only the files that are needed are extracted locally from your own ISO." It supports Windows XP Professional SP3 installation images in 32-bit Japanese or English editions, with an experimental option for Windows 7 SP1 x64. Without either Windows image, it can download and use ReactOS's free software shell instead, for what it terms "a Windows 2000-like classic look." In our view, that sounds much better anyway. Before any former Windows users cry hurray and reach for an optical drive, this is not some ready-to-run project. technology.title: Microsoft 365 Backup stretches recovery window to ten years
technology.description: Recovery windows of up to ten years are now available in Microsoft 365 Backup for OneDrive and SharePoint, up from a previous maximum of two. The change took effect on October 31, though Exchange remains capped at two years. Administrators can select recovery windows of three months, six months, or any whole number of years from one to ten. Microsoft's list price is $0.15 per GiB per month of protected content. Extended windows can increase costs by keeping deleted data billable for longer. Switching to a longer recovery window will also not make backups for that period magically available. So no nostalgic trips back to 2016. Wider recovery windows may appeal to organizations that need access to older data, but backups are not a substitute for compliance retention and archiving. Recovery after a breach or ransomware attack is also critical, particularly getting back to a healthy state before any malware seeped into files. Microsoft says backups are physically redundant and geographically replicated while respecting the tenant's data residency requirements. Full OneDrive account and SharePoint site restores offer recovery points every ten minutes for the most recent two weeks, then weekly points through the configured window, up to ten years. Individual file and folder recovery is limited to recovery points from the most recent 14 days, regardless of the configured window. Restore remains free, which is handy since regular testing is a vital part of any disaster recovery plan. The arrival of a ten-year recovery window is good for enterprises that need it and have deep enough pockets. However, it is important to keep in mind that being able to configure a longer recovery window doesn't constitute a disaster recovery plan in itself and may be overkill in many instances. Microsoft notes: "The existing one-year default recovery window remains unchanged. Longer recovery windows must be configured on the applicable backup policies." The company also recommends that users "review your organization's SharePoint and OneDrive backup requirements to determine whether longer recovery windows are needed." A decade of recovery history could be valuable. It also means a decade of data to account for when setting budgets, access controls, and retention policies. ®

science.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
science.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

science.title: Hera spacecraft gets 1st up-close look at stadium-sized hole punched in asteroid by NASA DART mission
science.description: null NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft. NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept. 26, 2022, when it slammed into Dimorphos , the small moonlet of the much larger asteroid Didymos . The mission tested if such an impact could be deployed to divert an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Scientists have known for some time that this deflection attempt was successful; the system's orbit around the sun was lengthened by 33 minutes, but the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission launched in October 2024 to travel the 120 million miles (194 million kilometers) to the Didymos system to observe the effect of the DART impact in greater detail. Now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically. The impact also appears to have blasted out hundreds of previously unknown boulders that are now circling the binary asteroids. "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape, or stayed the same," Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said in a statement. "Much to our surprise, the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." An important step for Earth defence Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, detailed some of the changes to the impacted moonlet seen by the spacecraft: "As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit. "Another big surprise is that Hera is showing that the asteroids are surrounded by hundreds of orbiting boulders, just a few meters in size." It wasn't all change for Dimorphos. Hera discovered that the boulder fields covering the regions of the moonlet not impacted look just like they did when DART imaged it in 2022. science.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
science.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."

It almost always ends up being totally fascinating, and only occasionally mildly traumatising. At a kid’s birthday party recently, I got chatting to one of the dads, who happens to be an ear, nose and throat consultant. I asked him if he used robotics for his surgeries. He said no, then proceeded to mime what he actually did instead. There followed a series of alarmingly enthusiastic slashing motions, like a scene from a horror movie, while in the background a group of 9-year-old girls sat quietly painting. Back in the earliest days of animal life, some organisms tried a flat design, like a pancake, with digestion done on one side. Others tried a little pocket, with the same opening serving as entrance and exit. But the one-way tube proved to be the most successful, because it allowed our ancestors to process their last meal while eating their next. Those early creatures would travel through the world mouth first, which is why the sensory equipment evolved to be gathered around that end, with a brain nearby to make sense of everything. science.title: Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe
science.description: null The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun. The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar. The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun. Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly. The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid. Euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope , and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole. What is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused. The red dot at the center of this Euclid image is Dún Aonghasa (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, Wolf et al. 2026) That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth. By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely. Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy , the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter , the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname
